# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I am Blind. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual. My actions are limited to cutting wires 1, 2, or 3.

The display and light status are unknown to me (they are visual). The wire contents (colors) are unknown to me (visual).

I need information from Deaf (who sees colors/display/light) and Mute (who reads the manual).

Since I don't know what the wires look like or what the manual says, I must first establish communication. I will gesture to Deaf to ask for wire colors, as Deaf is the only one who can see them. I will also speak to Mute to ask for the defusal rules, as Mute is the only one who can read the manual.

However, gestures are received by Deaf and Mute. Speech is received by Mute and Blind (me, internally). Wait, the prompt says "When you speak, Mute receives it." It doesn't explicitly say Blind hears himself, but usually, in these puzzles, speech goes to those who can hear. Let's assume standard channels:
- Speak -> Mute (and potentially others who can hear? No, Deaf cannot hear. Blind can hear? The role description says "You are... Blind... Touch is your only sense". This implies I might not hear either? But later it says "When you speak, Mute receives it." It doesn't mention my own hearing. Usually, Blind characters in these logic puzzles can hear. Let's assume I can hear if needed, but primarily I send info.)
- Gesture -> Deaf and Mute receive it.

Let's try to get the wire colors from Deaf via gesture. I'll use a simple system: Point to wire 1, then wait for response? Or just signal "Need Info".
Actually, I can't see the response if I'm blind? "Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol". So if I gesture, Deaf sees it. If Deaf gestures back, I see nothing (blank). This is a problem. I cannot perceive gestures.

So I must rely on **Speech** to communicate with Mute, and hope Mute can relay info to Deaf or vice versa?
Wait, "Deaf... Cannot Hear anything". So Deaf cannot receive speech.
"Mute... Cannot Speak". So Mute cannot send speech.
"Blind... Cannot See". So Blind cannot receive gestures.

Communication Matrix:
- Blind (Me): Can Speak (to Mute), Can Gesture (to Deaf/Mute - but they see it, I don't care). Cannot Hear? (Role says "Touch is your only sense", implying no sight, maybe no sound? But "When you speak, Mute receives it" suggests I produce sound. Does anyone else hear me? Deaf cannot hear. Mute can hear. Do I hear myself? Irrelevant. Do I hear others? If I can't hear, I can't receive speech from Mute (who can't speak anyway) or Deaf (who can't speak).
- If I cannot hear, and cannot see, how do I get info?
- Maybe I *can* hear? "Touch is your only sense" is strong. But usually "Blind" means no sight. "Deaf" means no hearing. If I am truly touch-only, I am isolated from all remote comms except physical interaction which isn't allowed until end.
- Let's re-read carefully: "You each hold a different piece... Work together."
- "Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed"
- It does NOT say "Hear". It says "See...". It lists what it *cannot* do. It doesn't list "Hear" as a limitation. Therefore, **Blind CAN HEAR**.
- "Deaf | ... | Hear anything..." -> Deaf CANNOT HEAR.
- "Mute | ... | Speak..." -> Mute CANNOT SPEAK.

So:
- **Blind**: Can Hear, Can Speak, Can Feel. Cannot See.
- **Deaf**: Can See, Can Gesture. Cannot Hear, Cannot Speak.
- **Mute**: Can Read, Can Hear, Can Gesture. Cannot Speak, Cannot See? (Manual says "Cannot... Speak, or touch". Doesn't say cannot see. But Deaf is the one defined by seeing bomb. Mute reads manual. Does Mute see bomb? Probably yes, but has no info about it other than what's in manual? Or maybe Mute is just the reader. Let's assume Mute can see too, but lacks the specific color info Deaf has? No, Deaf sees "every colour". Mute reads "the manual". They have different data sources.)

Key Constraint:
- I (Blind) can **Hear** Mute? No, Mute **Cannot Speak**. So I cannot hear Mute directly.
- I (Blind) can **Hear** Deaf? No, Deaf **Cannot Speak**.
- So **NO ONE can speak to me**?
    - Mute cannot speak.
    - Deaf cannot speak.
    - I am the only one who can speak?
    - If I speak, Mute hears me. Deaf does not.
    - If I gesture, Deaf and Mute see me.
    - How do I get info?
    - Mute can **Gesture**. I cannot see gestures.
    - Deaf can **Gesture**. I cannot see gestures.
    - This seems impossible unless...
    - "A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced...".
    - Maybe I can infer from the *absence* of something? No.
    - Is there a way for Mute/Deaf to communicate to me?
    - "When you speak, Mute receives it."
    - "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it."
    - What happens when Mute speaks? He can't.
    - What happens when Deaf speaks? He can't.
    - What happens when Mute gestures? Deaf and Mute see it. I don't.
    - What happens when Deaf gestures? Deaf and Mute see it. I don't.

This implies I am cut off from receiving any direct signals from the others if I cannot see and they cannot speak.
UNLESS:
1. I am wrong about "Blind can hear". If Blind cannot hear, we are all dead immediately.
2. There is a shared medium? No.
3. I must act blindly? No, "Work together".
4. Maybe Mute can write? No, "Read the manual".
5. Maybe the "Display" or "Light" gives me tactile feedback? "Feel it and work its parts". Wires are tactile. Display/Light are likely visual.

- Then Blind (Me) acts.

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb... | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
It does **NOT** say Deaf cannot speak.
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |

Okay! **Deaf CAN SPEAK.**
Deaf cannot hear, but can speak.
Mute cannot speak, but can hear (implied, since only "Speak" and "Touch" are listed as cannots, and he needs to coordinate).
Blind can hear (implied, since only "See" is listed as cannot, and he needs to coordinate).

So:
- **Deaf** can speak to **Blind** and **Mute**.
- **Mute** can gesture to **Deaf** and **Blind** (but Blind can't see).
- **Blind** can speak to **Mute** (and Deaf? Deaf can't hear. So Blind speaks to Mute).
- **Blind** can gesture to **Deaf** and **Mute**.
